label: Organ / Procedure
question: What organ and procedure does this specimen come from?
description: Identify the uterine specimen type from whole-slide architecture: a hysterectomy with full uterine wall and cavity, fragmented curettings/biopsy tissue, or oriented resection. Note overall tissue layout, amount, and orientation.

label: Compartment
question: Which uterine compartment shows the principal lesion?
description: Localize the principal lesion across uterine compartments: the endometrial lining, the myometrial smooth-muscle wall, the endomyometrial junctional zone, the serosa/perimetrial surface, or a discrete mass lesion. Assess which layer is most architecturally disturbed.

label: Endometrium
question: Which process best characterizes the endometrium?
description: Assess endometrial gland-to-stroma ratio, gland crowding, cytologic atypia, inflammation, and surface architecture to separate physiologic cycling endometrium, atrophic endometrium, endometritis, polyp, hyperplasia, and carcinoma.

label: Cycle phase
question: Which menstrual cycle phase does the endometrium reflect?
description: Evaluate glandular morphology for cycle phasing: straight tubular mitotically active glands with pseudostratified nuclei (proliferative), tortuous glands with subnuclear vacuoles or luminal secretions and predecidualized stroma (secretory), or stromal breakdown with condensation and crumbling glands (menstrual).

label: Endometritis type
question: What type of inflammatory infiltrate is present in the endometrium?
description: Characterize the endometrial inflammatory infiltrate: neutrophils within gland lumina and microabscesses (acute), interstitial stromal plasma cells with spindled stroma (chronic), or granulomas with epithelioid histiocytes and giant cells (granulomatous).

label: Hyperplasia: atypia
question: Do the crowded hyperplastic glands show cytologic atypia?
description: Determine whether crowded back-to-back endometrial glands show cytologic atypia with rounded vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli (atypical hyperplasia / endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia) versus preserved bland cytology with reduced stroma (hyperplasia without atypia).

label: Carcinoma subtype
question: Which histologic subtype does the endometrial carcinoma show?
description: Subtype the endometrial carcinoma from architecture and cytology: confluent or cribriform glands with squamous morules (endometrioid), complex papillae with high-grade pleomorphic nuclei (serous), clear or hobnail cells with hyalinized cores (clear cell), a biphasic malignant epithelial-and-mesenchymal proliferation (carcinosarcoma), or sheets of anaplastic cells without differentiation (undifferentiated).

label: FIGO grade
question: What is the FIGO grade of the endometrial carcinoma?
description: Assign FIGO grade from the proportion of solid non-squamous/non-morular growth combined with nuclear atypia: predominantly glandular (grade 1), intermediate solid component (grade 2), or predominantly solid sheets with marked nuclear atypia (grade 3).

label: Background endometrium
question: What is the state of the non-neoplastic background endometrium?
description: Retrieve non-neoplastic endometrium away from the main carcinoma bulk and dominant tumor glands. Examine distant background endometrium for pathogenetic typing: thin inactive atrophic background (favors serous/type II), proliferative or estrogen-effect background, or hyperplastic background with crowded glands (favors endometrioid/type I). Avoid sampling tumor-rich ROIs.

label: Myometrium
question: What is the dominant myometrial process?
description: Assess the myometrial wall for circumscribed whorled smooth-muscle nodules (leiomyoma), ectopic endometrial glands and stroma within muscle (adenomyosis), an atypical infiltrative spindle-cell proliferation (leiomyosarcoma or endometrial stromal sarcoma), diffuse muscle hypertrophy, or degenerative/hyaline change.

label: Smooth-muscle tumor criteria
question: Which combination of malignancy criteria does the smooth-muscle tumor meet?
description: Apply the smooth-muscle malignancy triad to the spindle-cell tumor: diffuse moderate-to-severe cytologic atypia, elevated mitotic count, and coagulative tumor-cell necrosis. Separate benign leiomyoma (none), atypia alone, smooth-muscle tumor of uncertain malignant potential (borderline single criterion), and leiomyosarcoma (two or more criteria).

label: Junctional zone
question: What is the status of the endomyometrial junction?
description: Evaluate the endomyometrial junctional zone for endometrial glands and stroma extending deep into the myometrium with reactive smooth-muscle hypertrophy (adenomyosis) versus an intact regular junction without ectopic glands (normal).

label: Serosa / Perimetrium
question: What serosal or perimetrial finding is present?
description: Inspect the serosa and perimetrium for fibrous adhesions on the mesothelial surface, ectopic endometrial glands and stroma with hemosiderin-laden macrophages (endometriosis), or an unremarkable smooth mesothelial-lined surface.

label: Histologic type
question: What is the broad histologic type of the mass lesion?
description: Classify the discrete uterine mass by lineage: a gland-forming or solid epithelial proliferation (epithelial tumor), a spindled/round-cell stromal or muscle proliferation (mesenchymal tumor), a biphasic malignant epithelial-and-mesenchymal lesion (mixed Mullerian tumor), a trophoblastic proliferation with atypia (gestational trophoblastic disease), a deposit morphologically foreign to uterus (metastatic tumor), or another non-neoplastic lesion.

label: Microscopic pattern / architecture
question: What is the dominant microscopic growth pattern of the lesion?
description: Determine the dominant growth architecture of the lesion: gland-forming epithelial (glandular), spindled or round-cell stroma (stromal), interlacing fascicles of smooth muscle (smooth muscle), an admixture of architectures (mixed/complex), or destructive infiltration of surrounding tissue with irregular borders (infiltrative/destructive).

label: Cellular features
question: Which cytologic and cellular features are present in the lesion?
description: At high power in the lesional ROI, catalogue cytologic and tissue-level features: nuclear atypia with pleomorphism and prominent nucleoli, brisk mitotic activity including atypical mitoses, geographic tumor-cell necrosis, an inflammatory infiltrate, and hormonal/secretory effect on the epithelium. Prioritize patches with mitotic figures and necrosis when present.

label: Stage / Extent
question: What is the extent of the lesion?
description: Assess invasion depth and spread across the uterine wall. Retrieve the tumor-myometrium interface and invasion front: confined non-invasive or in-situ disease, superficial (inner-half) myometrial invasion, deep (outer-half) myometrial invasion, or extrauterine spread to serosa, adnexa, or vessels. Sample spatially distinct regions from the main tumor bulk when judging depth. Use not applicable for non-neoplastic processes.

label: Synthesis / Interpretation
question: Do the integrated findings support a single definitive diagnosis?
description: Integration node: weigh prior chain answers with thumbnail global context and any supporting H&E patches. Converge on a single diagnosis, a residual differential pending further work-up, or a descriptive interpretation. Patch retrieval targets representative lesional morphology, not abstract diagnostic labels.

label: Diagnosis
question: What is the final integrated diagnostic category?
description: Final integration category from accumulated chain evidence: benign, premalignant/precursor, malignant, non-neoplastic/reactive, or descriptive when a definitive category cannot be assigned. Retrieval is secondary; rely on thumbnail plus prior node answers.

label: Reporting
question: Generate the final structured pathology report.
description: Synthesize the prior chain steps into a CAP-format uterine pathology report covering specimen, diagnosis, histologic type/grade, and extent.
